questions.q: Standing before a great monument, the author reflected that no star, tree or animal could have built it. What did he go on to reason from man’s superiority over the rest of creation?
options: That monuments should be preserved
Not quite. The article says: If a higher order of being exists in man, a still higher Being – God – is entirely conceivable.
That man needs no one above him
Not quite. The article says: If a higher order of being exists in man, a still higher Being – God – is entirely conceivable.
If a higher order of being exists in man, a still higher Being – God – is entirely conceivable
Yes. Man is not the “full-stop” of the universe.
That animals lack feelings
Not quite. The article says: If a higher order of being exists in man, a still higher Being – God – is entirely conceivable.
questions.rationale: “When a higher state of existence is present in the form of man, then why should the existence of another higher state in the form of God not be a possibility?”

questions.q: A person earns his living and is content for a time, then feels something is missing. What does the article say he is really looking for?
options: Meaning – which is found in discovering God for oneself
Right. “Man does not live by bread alone.”
Wider fame
Not quite. The article says: Meaning – which is found in discovering God for oneself.
More leisure
Not quite. The article says: Meaning – which is found in discovering God for oneself.
A better-paid position
Not quite. The article says: Meaning – which is found in discovering God for oneself.
questions.rationale: “Bread can satisfy only one’s physical requirements; it fails to give any intellectual satisfaction, or add meaning to one’s life… everyone is in search of God.”

questions.q: What does the article give as the sign of having truly found God, and the one condition of the search?
options: Great learning; the condition is long study
Not quite. The article says: A peace like a child’s in its mother’s arms; the condition is sincerity.
Many followers; the condition is eloquence
Not quite. The article says: A peace like a child’s in its mother’s arms; the condition is sincerity.
Freedom from work; the condition is wealth
Not quite. The article says: A peace like a child’s in its mother’s arms; the condition is sincerity.
A peace like a child’s in its mother’s arms; the condition is sincerity
Well read. “The one who seeks finds.”
questions.rationale: “When you find Him, you will feel at peace with yourself and with the universe, like a little boy in the arms of his mother. The process of search has only one condition to it, and that is, sincerity.”

questions.q: We are certain of our own existence, yet the “I” cannot be observed. What does the article draw from this?
options: That only the body is real
Not quite. The article says: What we know by understanding rather than by sight can still be certain – and so it is with God.
That the self is an illusion
Not quite. The article says: What we know by understanding rather than by sight can still be certain – and so it is with God.
That nothing at all can be known
Not quite. The article says: What we know by understanding rather than by sight can still be certain – and so it is with God.
What we know by understanding rather than by sight can still be certain – and so it is with God
Yes. To deny one would mean denying the other.
questions.rationale: “The cognizance of ‘I’ is at the level of perception or comprehension, and not at the level of observation. Exactly the same is true of God.”

questions.q: Which modern example does the article use to make God’s unseen governance of the universe easier to grasp?
options: Lamps lit by a switch
Not quite. The article says: We ourselves direct machines in outer space by remote control.
We ourselves direct machines in outer space by remote control
Correct. If man can, why not the Creator?
Clocks that run without winding
Not quite. The article says: We ourselves direct machines in outer space by remote control.
Telephones that carry the voice
Not quite. The article says: We ourselves direct machines in outer space by remote control.
questions.rationale: “We, ourselves direct the movements of machines in outer space by means of remote control, so why should we have any difficulty in accepting that there is a God who controls the universe by His own invisible system?”

questions.q: In a violent storm at sea, a little girl played on calmly with her dolls. What was her explanation?
options: She had sailed many times before
Not quite. The article says: Her father was the captain, and he would not let the ship sink.
She did not know there was a storm
Not quite. The article says: Her father was the captain, and he would not let the ship sink.
She had been told to keep quiet
Not quite. The article says: Her father was the captain, and he would not let the ship sink.
Her father was the captain, and he would not let the ship sink
Yes. A believer trusts God as the captain of his life.
questions.rationale: “You know, my father is the captain of this ship. He is not going to let it sink.”

questions.q: On what, according to the article, is the love of God naturally based?
options: The habit of one’s family
Not quite. The article says: The discovery that one’s life and all that sustains it are gifts from Him.
A feeling that cannot be explained
Not quite. The article says: The discovery that one’s life and all that sustains it are gifts from Him.
Fear of punishment
Not quite. The article says: The discovery that one’s life and all that sustains it are gifts from Him.
The discovery that one’s life and all that sustains it are gifts from Him
Well reasoned. Love is acknowledgement of the Giver.
questions.rationale: “When one discovers this fact, one naturally feels a profound love for God. Thus, love of God is the outcome of one’s discovery of God’s munificence.”

questions.q: The chemical elements of a human body are worth very little in the market. What point does the article make with this?
options: That chemistry is a useless science
Not quite. The article says: From such ordinary matter God has made a living, thinking being beyond all price.
That human life is cheap
Not quite. The article says: From such ordinary matter God has made a living, thinking being beyond all price.
That the body should be neglected
Not quite. The article says: From such ordinary matter God has made a living, thinking being beyond all price.
From such ordinary matter God has made a living, thinking being beyond all price
Right. A lost hand or eye cannot be bought back.
questions.rationale: “Out of 12,000 rupees worth of matter, God has created a human being so wonderful that no price can be set upon him.”

questions.q: An astronaut said that standing on the moon made him feel God’s presence. What does the article say we must do to feel the same on earth?
options: Study astronomy
Not quite. The article says: Look at familiar things as if seeing them for the first time.
Wait for an unusual event
Not quite. The article says: Look at familiar things as if seeing them for the first time.
Travel to remote places
Not quite. The article says: Look at familiar things as if seeing them for the first time.
Look at familiar things as if seeing them for the first time
Exactly. Wonder is dulled by habit, not by distance.
questions.rationale: “We too have to look at everything—not as old and familiar—but as something new and exciting. We have to look at things as if we are seeing them for the first time.”

questions.q: The article contrasts a stuffed tiger in a museum with a living tiger in the forest. What two kinds of belief does this picture?
options: Traditional belief, which stirs nothing; and conscious, living belief, which shakes the whole person with awe
Well read. Only the second has value.
Belief of the learned and belief of the simple
Not quite. The article says: Traditional belief, which stirs nothing; and conscious, living belief, which shakes the whole person with awe.
Belief in private and belief in public
Not quite. The article says: Traditional belief, which stirs nothing; and conscious, living belief, which shakes the whole person with awe.
Belief of the young and belief of the old
Not quite. The article says: Traditional belief, which stirs nothing; and conscious, living belief, which shakes the whole person with awe.
questions.rationale: “A traditional belief in God is a lifeless belief… A conscious belief in God arises from discovering God in all His powers.”
